title: A release build can accept unchanged pre-existing manifest and zip files as proof of a new package
observed_behavior: The release service captures pre-run existence/fingerprints and returns manifest_preexisting, zip_preexisting, manifest_changed, and zip_changed, but release_build_evidence_errors checks only success plus post-run existence. A current-HEAD probe with success=true, both artifacts pre-existing, both changed flags false, and copy count zero returned ok=true, writes_release_package=true, no evidence errors, and 'manifest written; zip written.'
expected_invariant: A successful deployment-build result must prove that required artifacts belong to the current invocation, by creation/change evidence or a verified invocation/build identity, rather than accepting stale files that merely already exist.
root_cause: The build evidence policy never consumes the freshness fields already produced by release_result_payload; it treats path existence as sufficient proof after a zero exit code.
failure_scenario: A destination retains an older manifest and zip, then the builder exits zero without writing new output because of a silent early return or internal false-green. The Local API/UI reports a completed deployment package and writes_release_package=true while handing the operator stale artifacts.
evidence: command_policy.py lines 112-123 checks only success, manifest_exists, and requested zip_exists.
release.py lines 72-76 records pre-run fingerprints and release_result.py lines 55-62 computes current changed flags, so freshness evidence is available but ignored.
Isolated release_build_result probe: ok=true, writes_release_package=true, artifact_errors=[], manifest_changed=false, zip_changed=false, message says both artifacts were written.
All 46 focused maintenance/release tests pass; current tests cover missing artifacts and dry-run mutation, but the positive build fixture omits preexisting/freshness fields.
affected_flows: release progress and command journal evidence
operator selection of manifest/zip for distribution
existing_safeguards: Explicit confirm_create, active-work guard, maintenance lock, bounded subprocess timeout/tree termination, builder exit code, required artifact existence checks, optional builder verification, and pre/post fingerprints are present.
safeguard_gap: No current-invocation identity or creation/change requirement joins the exit code to the artifacts reported as newly written.
tests_missing: Successful zero-exit build with unchanged pre-existing manifest is rejected
Requested unchanged pre-existing zip is rejected
Fresh build identity or content fingerprint is tied to the current invocation
recommended_remediation: Require a newly created or demonstrably changed manifest and, when requested, zip; preferably validate a build/invocation identifier and file-set digest inside the manifest. Preserve explicit handling for destinations where unchanged reproducible bytes are legitimate by still requiring current-invocation proof.
remediation_risk: medium: reproducible builds can emit byte-identical artifacts, so simple mtime/size checks alone may false-block and an invocation-aware manifest field is safer
validation_rung: Focused release service/result/policy tests, disposable destination probes with stale and fresh artifacts, canonical release-policy gate, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current Python result-policy finding; related W10 findings concern builder-side cleanup/evidence/gate behavior rather than this stale-artifact acceptance path.

title: A limit-capped retention dry run reports ready without disclosing that most roots were never scanned
observed_behavior: The global limit stops category/root traversal as soon as enough candidate rows are collected, but the payload has no truncated, scan_complete, limit_reached, or omitted-count field and sets overall_status to ready whenever no OSError was recorded. With four log files and limit=1, the probe returned candidate_count=1, overall_status=ready, and no truncation evidence; every later category had zero roots_scanned.
expected_invariant: A bounded inventory must distinguish a complete scan from a partial sample, identify which roots/categories were not scanned, and avoid a ready/comprehensive status when the candidate cap was reached.
root_cause: remaining is used solely as an early-break counter. Completeness state is never recorded, while overall_status is derived only from scan_errors.
failure_scenario: An operator requests or defaults to a low cap on a runtime tree containing many artifacts. The report says ready and summarizes only the first category, leading the operator to underestimate cleanup volume and miss failure/cache/state categories entirely.
evidence: retention.py lines 27-40 shares one remaining counter across all categories; lines 304-330 break before later roots once it reaches zero.
retention.py lines 49-54 derives review/ready solely from errors and lines 55-85 emit no completion/truncation field.
Isolated temp-tree probe with four log files and limit=1 returned ready, one candidate, has_truncation=false, and empty roots_scanned for jsonl_state, temp/scratch, failure, and cache categories.
The focused retention tests pass but use limit 100/25 with only six candidates and do not exercise cap exhaustion.
affected_flows: operator cleanup planning and capacity estimates
future promotion of dry-run evidence into an apply workflow
existing_safeguards: The route is read-only, mutation_route_available=false, candidate rows are allowlist/exclusion checked, traversal is lazily bounded, and root-level OSError values produce review status.
safeguard_gap: The cap bounds work but its incompleteness is invisible, so the safe bound doubles as a false-completeness signal.
tests_missing: Limit exhaustion returns partial/truncated status and unscanned-root evidence
A later category remains visibly pending rather than appearing as zero candidates
Default-limit saturation is surfaced to the operator
recommended_remediation: Track limit exhaustion and per-category scan completion, emit scan_complete/truncated and unscanned roots/categories, and set overall_status to partial/review when the cap is reached. Keep the existing hard cap and read-only boundary.
remediation_risk: low: additive evidence fields and status refinement do not alter filesystem behavior, though frontend status handling must accept partial
validation_rung: Focused retention unit/API tests with cap exhaustion and multiple categories, bounded large-tree probe, WebView maintenance rendering checks, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New current-hash operational-completeness finding; no prior retention path finding was present.

title: Support exports created in the same second overwrite one another
observed_behavior: Export filenames use a UTC stamp with one-second precision and the atomic writer replaces an existing destination. A deterministic two-call probe with different request markers and the same stamp returned the same path for both calls; the surviving file contained only the second marker.
expected_invariant: Each successful support-export command should preserve its own diagnostic snapshot or explicitly report that it replaced a prior artifact.
root_cause: utc_file_stamp omits sub-second entropy and write_support_export does not allocate a collision-free suffix or use exclusive creation before os.replace.
failure_scenario: Two rapid API invocations, automation retries, or distinct commands within one second both report success and the same export path; the first incident snapshot is silently lost.
evidence: productization.py lines 57-58 formats only YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ; line 607 derives the complete filename from that value.
_write_json_atomically uses os.replace, so an existing same-name export is overwritten without warning.
Isolated temp AppData probe with utc_file_stamp fixed to one value: same_path=true and the final JSON request marker was 'second'.
Focused productization/maintenance tests pass; none creates two exports at the same timestamp.
affected_flows: command result log_paths and operator handoff
existing_safeguards: Exports are backend-owned, written atomically under DiagnosticsExports, maintenance commands are locked within one facade instance, and command results return the path.
safeguard_gap: The lock prevents simultaneous execution in one process but not sequential same-second calls, retries, other processes, or filename reuse; replacement is silent.
tests_missing: Two same-stamp exports receive distinct paths
recommended_remediation: Allocate filenames with microseconds plus an exclusive/random suffix or retry an O_EXCL-style unique candidate; never silently replace a prior support export.
remediation_risk: low: filename shape changes may require tests/UI expectations to accept a longer suffix
validation_rung: Focused productization/support-export tests, deterministic collision probe, Local API command test, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current operational evidence-retention finding; redaction/security behavior was intentionally not expanded.

title: Any internal TypeError causes completed-backfill dry run to execute a second time and can hide the first failure
observed_behavior: The facade treats every TypeError from the checkpoint-aware call as proof that the service has an old signature and retries without checkpoint_path. A probe whose first invocation raised an internal TypeError after starting work and whose second returned success showed two full calls and an overall successful result with an empty checkpoint path.
expected_invariant: Signature compatibility must be decided before invocation or limited to a proven unexpected-keyword mismatch; an exception raised inside the operation must fail once and remain visible, never trigger a duplicate expensive operation.
root_cause: The broad except TypeError surrounds the entire backfill call and cannot distinguish Python argument binding failure from implementation/runtime TypeError.
failure_scenario: A parser, callback, or checkpoint writer raises TypeError after scanning or writing evidence. The facade reruns the complete dry-run, potentially writes duplicate/discordant checkpoint evidence, and reports success if the second pass happens not to fail, hiding the original defect.
evidence: backfill_facade.py lines 35-49 catch all TypeError and re-invoke the same service without checkpoint_path.
Corrected isolated facade probe returned calls=2 with first keyword set including checkpoint_path, second without it, ok=true, and checkpoint_path empty after an internal TypeError.
The focused 46-test maintenance suite passes; current tests exercise the modern checkpoint call but not an internal TypeError or a legacy callable preflight.
The existing CSW-2026-07-09-MAINTENANCE-002 concerns operator copy about intentional checkpoint writes, not duplicate invocation or exception masking.
affected_flows: maintenance command result and progress trust
existing_safeguards: The operation is forced dry_run=true, a maintenance lock serializes facade calls, timeout is bounded, and completed-manifest mutation is prohibited by the service contract.
safeguard_gap: Dry-run still performs potentially long scans and evidence writes, and the facade can both repeat them and erase the first failure from the returned result.
tests_missing: Internal TypeError is returned as failure with exactly one invocation
Legacy no-checkpoint signature is detected without executing a failing first call
First-pass checkpoint side effects cannot be hidden by a retry
recommended_remediation: Inspect the callable signature/capability explicitly or introduce a versioned service contract. If a narrow compatibility retry must remain, retry only a confirmed argument-binding error before any service body executes and preserve the original exception in evidence.
remediation_risk: low-medium: legacy service doubles may rely on the fallback, so migrate them with an explicit capability test
validation_rung: Focused facade/service/API backfill tests including call counts and TypeError interleavings, checkpoint evidence assertions, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New root cause distinct from the existing dry-run checkpoint-copy finding on the same path.

title: Replacement failure after a journal move is reported as if nothing moved and omits the surviving archive path
observed_behavior: The archive helper moves the live journal first and then creates an empty replacement. If replacement creation fails, the outer catch appends only an error/skipped row and never records the already-completed move. A deterministic failure probe left the original path absent and the archived file intact, while the payload reported moved_count=0, moved_journals=[], and no archive_path.
expected_invariant: A multi-step evidence mutation must either roll back to the original state or truthfully report every completed step and recovery location, especially when the runtime journal path is now missing.
root_cause: The move and replacement are not transactional, and the archive result object containing archive_path is constructed only after write_text succeeds; exceptions discard knowledge of the chosen archive path.
failure_scenario: Disk quota, ACL, antivirus, or filesystem failure prevents creation of the fresh journal after the old one was moved. The operator sees 'archive failed' with zero moved, cannot discover the preserved archive from command evidence, and the runtime resumes with its expected journal path missing.
evidence: state_journal_archive.py lines 167-178 performs stat, mkdir, move, then write_text before returning archive metadata.
Lines 37-45 catch the later exception and append the pre-move candidate as skipped, losing archive_path and partial-success state.
Isolated temp probe forced Path.write_text to raise after move: original_exists=false, one archive retained the event content, but moved_count=0 and moved_journals was empty.
The current happy-path facade test confirms confirmation/close-readiness and successful move/replacement, but no failure-interleaving test exists.
existing_safeguards: Strict facade confirmation, safe close-readiness requirement, filename/state-root eligibility checks, minimum-size threshold, unique archive filenames, maintenance lock, and preservation of the moved bytes all reduce harm.
safeguard_gap: No rollback or partial-success record covers the interval after move and before replacement creation, so state and evidence disagree exactly on the failure path.
tests_missing: Replacement creation failure after successful move reports archive_path and original absence
Safe rollback restores the original when replacement creation fails
Restart behavior when pipeline_events.jsonl is absent after partial archive
recommended_remediation: Stage and fsync a replacement before committing the move where filesystem semantics permit, or rollback the archive move on replacement failure. At minimum construct/retain partial-result evidence immediately after move, including archive_path, replacement_created=false, and an explicit recovery action.
remediation_risk: medium: journal writers and Windows rename/open-handle behavior require deterministic interleaving tests and close-readiness preservation
validation_rung: Focused archive facade/unit tests with injected move/write failures, restart/journal-writer recovery test, filesystem evidence assertions, and strict change-packet coverage; representative real media is not required.
prior_audit_relationship: New exact-current operational failure-interleaving finding; no prior finding was located on this path.
